concepts.def: A mapping f: X → Y assigning exactly one y to each x in the domain X. Written y = f(x).
Domain is the set of valid inputs; range is the set of outputs produced. For f(x)=√x, domain x≥0, range f(x)≥0.
fg(x) means apply g first, then f: fg(x) = f(g(x)). Order matters; fg(x) ≠ gf(x) in general.
f⁻¹ reverses f: f(f⁻¹(x)) = x. Exists only if f is one-to-one. Domain of f⁻¹ = range of f.
|x| = x if x≥0, else −x. Graph is V-shaped, vertex at origin. |f(x)|=k gives two equations: f(x)=±k.
y = f(x)+a translates up by a; y = f(x+a) translates left by a; y = af(x) stretches vertically; y = f(ax) compresses horizontally.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Algebra & Functions — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Algebra & Functions brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Algebra & Functions.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: If f(x) = 2x + 1 and g(x) = x², what is fg(3)?
Which is the inverse of f(x) = 3x − 5?
What is the value of x^0 (for x not equal to zero)?
options: x^0 equals 0 because raising something to the zero gives nothing.
x^0 equals x because the zero has no effect.
x^(1/2) means 1 divided by x squared.
1 — any non-zero number to the power of zero equals 1.
x^(1/2) means 1 divided by x squared.
x^(1/2) means x divided by 2 — half of x.
x^0 equals x because the zero has no effect.
The square root of x (the positive root when x is positive).
(-3)^2 equals -6 because the negative makes you subtract.
9 — squaring a negative gives a positive.
x^0 equals x because the zero has no effect.
(-3)^2 equals -9 because the minus is preserved.
